paragraphs: The European Union needs money for its next long budget. This budget is for the years 2028 to 2034. It pays for many things, like help for farmers and poorer regions.
EU leaders cannot agree on it. Some of them now want a new way to get money.
One idea is to take some of the new tax that big companies pay. Ireland gets a lot of this tax.
Ireland now asks very big companies to pay a little more tax. This could bring about €5 billion a year.
France likes the idea. But Irish officials say there is no clear plan yet. EU leaders will meet in Dublin next week.
sentZh: 歐盟的下一個長期預算需要錢。
這個預算涵蓋2028年到2034年。
它支付許多事情，例如幫助農民和較貧窮的地區。
歐盟領袖無法達成一致。
其中一些人現在想要一種新的方式來取得資金。
一個想法是拿走大公司所繳新稅的一部分。
愛爾蘭收到很多這種稅。
愛爾蘭現在要求非常大的公司多繳一點稅。
這每年可能帶來大約50億歐元。
法國喜歡這個想法。
但愛爾蘭官員說目前還沒有明確的計畫。
歐盟領袖下週將在都柏林開會。

paragraphs: The European Union is finding it hard to agree on its next long-term budget, which will cover the years 2028 to 2034. Now, some EU leaders are looking at Ireland's corporate tax money as a possible way to pay for it.

António Costa, the president of the European Council, wants to find new sources of money that go straight to Brussels. Reports say his team is thinking about taking part of the extra tax that comes from a recent international deal on a minimum tax rate for big companies.

Ireland charges companies 12.5% tax, but very large companies now pay an extra 2.5%, so they pay 15% in total. Ireland's Fiscal Council thinks this extra tax could bring in about €5 billion, around 13% of this year's corporate tax.
Officials in Dublin say the idea has been discussed, but there is no firm plan yet. France strongly supports it. The issue may come up when EU leaders meet in Dublin next week.
sentZh: 歐盟難以就下一個涵蓋2028至2034年的長期預算達成一致。
現在，一些歐盟領袖正把愛爾蘭的公司稅收入視為可能的財源。
歐洲理事會主席安東尼奧·科斯塔希望找到直接流向布魯塞爾的新財源。
報導指出，他的團隊正考慮拿走一項關於大公司最低稅率的近期國際協議所帶來的額外稅收的一部分。
愛爾蘭向公司課徵12.5%的稅，但非常大的公司現在要多繳2.5%，總共繳15%。
愛爾蘭財政諮詢委員會認為，這筆額外稅收每年可帶來約50億歐元，約佔今年公司稅的13%。
都柏林的官員說這個想法已被討論過，但還沒有確定的計畫。
法國強烈支持。
歐盟領袖下週在都柏林開會時，這個議題可能會被提出。

paragraphs: As the European Union struggles to agree its next seven-year budget, covering 2028 to 2034, Ireland's corporate tax revenue has once again attracted attention in Brussels.

European Council president António Costa is searching for new 'own resources', money that flows directly to the EU rather than through national governments. According to reports, his team has considered redirecting part of the extra revenue generated by the recent OECD agreement on a global minimum tax.

Ireland has a 12.5% corporate tax rate, but large companies now pay an additional 2.5% top-up to meet the 15% minimum. The Fiscal Council estimates this top-up could raise around €5 billion, roughly 13% of the corporate tax expected this year.

Sources in Dublin confirm the idea has been raised but insist there is no formal proposal. France is strongly in favour, and the issue could feature at an informal summit of EU leaders in Dublin next week, ahead of a crucial meeting in Brussels at the end of the month.
sentZh: 在歐盟努力就涵蓋2028至2034年的下一個七年預算達成協議之際，愛爾蘭的公司稅收入再次引起布魯塞爾的關注。
歐洲理事會主席安東尼奧·科斯塔正在尋找新的「自有財源」，也就是直接流向歐盟而非經過各國政府的資金。
據報導，他的團隊曾考慮把近期OECD全球最低稅協議所產生的額外稅收的一部分轉用。
愛爾蘭的公司稅率為12.5%，但大公司現在需額外支付2.5%的附加稅以達到15%的最低標準。
財政諮詢委員會估計，這項附加稅可帶來約50億歐元，約為今年預期公司稅的13%。
都柏林的消息人士證實這個想法已被提出，但堅稱並沒有正式提案。
法國強烈贊成，這個議題可能出現在下週於都柏林舉行的歐盟領袖非正式峰會上，也就是月底布魯塞爾關鍵會議之前。

paragraphs: With the European Union locked in difficult negotiations over its 2028 to 2034 budget, Ireland's lucrative corporate tax receipts have once more come under scrutiny in Brussels.

European Council president António Costa is hunting for fresh 'own resources', revenue that bypasses national treasuries and flows straight into EU coffers. His team has reportedly floated the notion of siphoning off a portion of the windfall generated by the recent OECD deal on a global minimum tax.

Although Ireland's headline rate remains 12.5%, the largest firms now pay a 2.5% top-up to reach the 15% floor. The Fiscal Council reckons this could yield in the region of €5 billion, approximately 13% of this year's anticipated corporate tax take.

Officials in Dublin acknowledge the idea has been aired but stress that nothing concrete is on the table. France is a vocal backer, and the matter may surface at an informal gathering of EU leaders in Dublin next week, in the run-up to a pivotal Brussels summit at the end of the month.
sentZh: 隨著歐盟陷入2028至2034年預算的艱難談判，愛爾蘭豐厚的公司稅收入再度在布魯塞爾受到審視。
歐洲理事會主席安東尼奧·科斯塔正在尋覓新的「自有財源」，即繞過各國國庫、直接流入歐盟金庫的收入。
據報導，他的團隊已提出從近期OECD全球最低稅協議所帶來的意外之財中抽走一部分的構想。
儘管愛爾蘭的名義稅率仍為12.5%，最大的企業現在需支付2.5%的附加稅以達到15%的下限。
財政諮詢委員會估計，這可能帶來約50億歐元，約為今年預期公司稅收的13%。
都柏林官員承認這個想法曾被提出，但強調目前並無具體方案。
法國是大力支持者，此事可能在下週於都柏林舉行的歐盟領袖非正式聚會上浮現，也就是月底布魯塞爾關鍵峰會的前夕。

paragraphs: As the European Union continues to negotiate its multiannual budget for the period 2028 to 2034, Ireland's corporate tax revenue has once again become a focus of attention among European policymakers.

The President of the European Council, António Costa, is seeking to establish new 'own resources', namely revenue streams that are transferred directly to the EU budget. It has been reported that his team is considering the reallocation of a proportion of the additional revenue arising from the recent OECD agreement on a global minimum corporate tax.

Although Ireland's standard rate remains 12.5%, large multinational companies are now subject to a 2.5% top-up in order to comply with the 15% minimum. The Fiscal Council estimates that this could generate approximately €5 billion, equivalent to roughly 13% of anticipated corporate tax receipts this year.

Nevertheless, officials in Dublin maintain that, although the concept has been discussed, no formal proposal currently exists. France is a strong proponent of the measure; consequently, it may be raised at an informal summit of EU leaders in Dublin next week, prior to a decisive meeting in Brussels at the end of the month.

歐洲理事會主席安東尼奧·科斯塔正尋求建立新的「自有財源」，即直接轉入歐盟預算的收入來源。
據報導，他的團隊正考慮將近期OECD全球最低公司稅協議所產生的部分額外收入重新分配。
儘管愛爾蘭的標準稅率仍為12.5%，大型跨國公司現在須繳納2.5%的附加稅以符合15%的最低標準。
財政諮詢委員會估計，這可帶來約50億歐元，相當於今年預期公司稅收的約13%。
然而，都柏林官員堅稱，雖然這個構想已被討論，但目前並無正式提案。
法國是這項措施的堅定支持者；因此，這個議題可能在下週於都柏林舉行的歐盟領袖非正式峰會上被提出，時間在月底布魯塞爾的決定性會議之前。

paragraphs: As the European Union struggles to agree its next seven-year budget, covering 2028 to 2034, Ireland's corporate tax revenue has once again attracted attention in Brussels.

European Council president António Costa is searching for new 'own resources', money that flows directly to the EU rather than through national governments. According to reports, his team has considered redirecting part of the extra revenue generated by the recent OECD agreement on a global minimum tax.

Ireland has a 12.5% corporate tax rate, but large companies now pay an additional 2.5% top-up to meet the 15% minimum. The Fiscal Council estimates this top-up could raise around €5 billion, roughly 13% of the corporate tax expected this year.

Sources in Dublin confirm the idea has been raised but insist there is no formal proposal. France is strongly in favour, and the issue could feature at an informal summit of EU leaders in Dublin next week, ahead of a crucial meeting in Brussels at the end of the month.
